topic: Particle model of solids, liquids, and gases
key_concepts: Particles in solids are tightly packed in a regular, repeating crystalline structure.
Solid particles have very little empty space between them, contributing to high density.
Solid particles vibrate in fixed positions, which gives solids rigidity and a fixed shape.
Liquid particles are close together but randomly arranged rather than ordered.
Liquid particles have slightly greater spacing than solids, allowing them to flow past one
Liquids take the shape of their container but maintain a relatively constant volume.
Gas particles are widely spaced, have no fixed arrangement, and are randomly dispersed.
Gas particles move rapidly in all directions and collide with each other and container wal
Gases fill the entire volume of their container and have no fixed shape or volume.
Solid particles have the lowest kinetic energy, liquids have more, and gases have the most
Intermolecular forces are strong in solids, weaker in liquids, and very weak or negligible
